title: incident-bot: on-call diagnostics contextual links and quick-fix suggestions
author: Ava Patel
description: Motivation: On-call engineers need faster, richer context when incident-bot suggests SLO diagnostics. This PR adds contextual quick-links (runbooks, recent deploys, SLO graphs) and a small 'quick-fix' suggestions section surfaced inline in on-call notifications. The goal is to reduce mean-time-to-resolution by making the most relevant artifacts available immediately. Implementation summary: backend enrichment of diagnostic payloads, Slack/console formatter updates, and UI helpers to render contextual links and up to 3 suggested actions. The feature is behind an org-scoped feature flag 'oncall_context_links'. Checklist: - Add diagnostics_context enrichment endpoint and payload fields - Add renderers/formatters for Slack and Console - Emit telemetry for clicks and actions - Add unit and integration tests - Update docs and migration notes - Rollout plan and metrics. How it works: the diagnostics service attaches a flat diagnostics_context map with keys: runbook_url, last_successful_deploy, slo_graph_url, recent_errors_sample, suggested_actions (list). Formatters render inline contextual links and a suggested actions block with optional one-click 'Open runbook' behaviour. Telemetry: diagnostics.click and diagnostics.action_taken events are emitted to Snowplow with org_id, incident_id, suggested_action_id. Backwards compatibility: older clients will ignore the extra fields; change is behind flag so rollout is incremental. Performance: enrichment is done lazily and batched for multi-incident summaries to avoid extra latency on hot paths. Testing: unit tests for enrichment and formatter, integration tests against a mock slo-toolkit, end-to-end validation in staging. Related work: ENG-4823 (on-call experience improvements), SRE-719 (SLO toolkit quick actions). Migration notes: no DB schema changes; consumers should tolerate missing fields; enable flag per-org in Console. Rollout: gated rollout over 1 week with click-through and false-positive suggestion rates monitored.
